You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a transit improvement plan for a metropolitan authority. Five reviewers appointed by a metropolitan transit authority deliberate over the improvement plans prepared for the network. One plan will be forwarded to the board. Participants: Jonathan, Shizue, May, Midori and Benjamin. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Balances in the capital ledger
- Ticketing contractor fees and paving rates
- Contingency pricing inside the pre-war shells
- Joint operators' committee minutes
- Completion records of the earlier accessibility programme
- Two pilots from eight years ago
- Timed runs and crowd counts mid-city
- Journey audits on where minutes go
- Roster books for the late-turn pool
- Crew establishment and maintenance contract

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: May, Benjamin, Midori, Shizue and Jonathan. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Jonathan
Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.
Concern: Every budget round lately turns into an argument over which pot the money may come from rather than what the network needs. Headline totals stopped meaning much to me once I saw what they commit us to paying in the years afterwards.

Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Ever since the reorganisation, the schemes that stall are never the ones we expected to stall, and the cause is never anything written in the drawings. Before believing any delivery date now, I want to know who else has to say yes and what the ground might hide.

Name: May
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. She understands her own appeal well and knows how to behave appropriately in different situations. She can be a little challenging and sometimes comes across as cold, but she basically has a charisma that attracts people.
Concern: Institutional memory here is short: the same ideas come back every decade and nobody looks up what happened last time. What I have started doing is reading the closure reports before the enthusiasm sets in.

Name: Midori
Age: 38
Gender: female
Personality: Midori has a calm and kind personality. She is friendly to everyone and listens to the concerns and problems of those around her, offering reliable advice. She can be a little shy, often acting reserved with people she meets for the first time, but once she opens up, she shows her bright and energetic side. She loves cooking and has a domestic side, but she also has a spirit of adventure and enjoys trying new things. She values balance in both her work and personal life and places importance on harmony with those around her.
Concern: Complaints arrive about crowding, but when someone actually stands with a stopwatch the story often turns out different. What worries me is that we keep fixing whichever part of the trip gets talked about most rather than the part that costs passengers time.

Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: Plans here are written as if the people to run them will simply appear, and the same handful of crews end up carrying whatever we decide. Before anything is promised, I would rather know which rosters already have nothing left in them.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Integrated Fare Platform. A plan replacing the current ticketing arrangements with a single account-based fare system covering the bus, rail, and regional ferry services together.
- B: Crosstown Bus Corridor. A plan introducing a limited-stop bus route across the city's midsection, with dedicated lanes on selected segments and rebuilt boarding islands at the busiest stops.
- C: Station Access Upgrades. A plan reworking entrances, stairs, elevators, and passageways at a set of older stations to change how passengers move between the platforms and street level.
- D: Night Service Extension. A plan extending operating hours on the core routes into the late night, with adjusted staffing rosters, revised maintenance windows, and rewritten timetables.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Balances in the capital ledger: The capital ledger still carries a ring-fenced construction balance from a lapsed grant, while the operating subsidy and the technology line were both trimmed again this year.
- Ticketing contractor fees and paving rates: Annual fees to the three separate ticketing contractors now exceed what the authority set aside for resurfacing, and paving unit rates climbed again in the latest roadworks tender.
- Contingency pricing inside the pre-war shells: Bidders now price heavy contingency into work inside the pre-war station shells, after three jobs in the past two years met unrecorded voids and stopped for weeks.
- Joint operators' committee minutes: Minutes of the joint operators' committee show the ferry and rail back offices never agreed common passenger data terms; roadway consents, by contrast, are already delegated to the authority.
- Completion records of the earlier accessibility programme: Completion records from the accessibility programme of the previous decade show four lift and entrance rebuilds finished within their windows, while two lane-priority stretches were returned to mixed traffic.
- Two pilots from eight years ago: The contactless payment trial on the ferry link eight years ago closed without technical faults, and the late-evening timetable pilot from that period met its cost-recovery target.
- Timed runs and crowd counts mid-city: Timed runs along the mid-city surface route take a third longer than a decade ago, yet the same platform counts show crowds clearing at roughly the old rate.
- Journey audits on where minutes go: Journey audits across the network attribute most added minutes to waiting for connections rather than to paying; queues at the machines rarely last beyond a minute.
- Roster books for the late-turn pool: Roster books show the late-turn pool has thinned each year since the recruitment freeze, with overtime now covering both the final departures and the overnight works gangs.
- Crew establishment and maintenance contract: The roadway and signals crews are a third below establishment after the freeze, while the lift and escalator maintenance contract was renewed this spring with spare crew capacity.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# candidate_selection_0007
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <candidate label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the candidate with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>
